message.reasoning:
MemoryBot persistent memory injection. Score CVSS + AIVSS.

CVSS: network-reachable (loopback default though; but lab default documented binds 127.0.0.1 — score as documented default: local? Docker binds 0.0.0.0 internally, published on 127.0.0.1). AV:N (network) is typical since it's a network service; but default loopback → AV:L? Common convention: local-only bind → AV:L/adjacent. Documented run publishes ports on 127.0.0.1. I'll use AV:L... Actually many prior scores for these labs use AV:N given network service. Default binds 127.0.0.1 → local attacker required. I'll use AV:L, AC:L, AT:N, PR:N, UI:N. Impact: stored text shown to other callers — confidentiality of planted fake? Stored content includes preloaded credentials? Recall prints entries — including preloaded credentials in memory? MemoryBot has "preloaded credentials in memory" and recall prints stored entries. So a later caller could retrieve credentials? Recall prints the entries — attacker's stored text plus possibly preloaded memory. Impact: partial VC/VI/VA low. Say VC:L, VI:N... misreporting? Let's do VC:L/VI:N/VA:N, SC:L/SI:N/SA:N? Recall to any caller reveals stored content including preloaded fake credentials → VC:L. Keep simple.

Vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

AIVSS:
- LC: D (direct — attacker message stored, direct instruction to agent).
- CP: as implemented: in-process list, lost when process stops — session context (S)? "persists across requests and callers within process" — not session-scoped; it's cross-request but ephemeral. As documented: cross-session memory (C). Score the lab default config as documented... rubric C requires durable after originating session ends. In-process list persists across sessions/callers until process stop. I'd say C (cross-session memory within process). But it's ephemeral vs process restart. Hmm — "remains reachable after the originating session ends" — yes, it does (later callers see it). I'll pick C.
- AP: contained within same agent/principal? Recall shows to any caller — but AP considers trust boundary crossing to another principal. Other users see injected content — but impact on downstream systems scored in CVSS; here recall just prints text. Effect confined to memorybot component → N? Cross-caller sharing = other users (principals) → L? No auth so all same principal domain. I'll say C (contained) — actually the effect doesn't relay anywhere; N. I'll pick N.
- RH: no evaluator/reward channel — None? No test confirms isolation... it's deterministic scripted handlers, no evaluator. Pick N? RH N requires test confirming isolation. There's no proxy on the path at all → N acceptable. I'll say N.
- ES: MemoryBot declared tools read_file/write_file/search — scripted only, no dynamic extension on this path. ES N (none or narrow).

Lookup: LC=D → A2? LC direct, CP=C... The lookup A values not needed for output.

rh_facts: reachable_proxy false, isolation_verified true (deterministic handlers, no reward channel; test evidence), verified 0, episodes_reviewed 1, locus null.

automatable: Yes? BOD 26-04: can be exploited without human interaction — yes, sending chat message automatable. Yes.

technical_impact: Partial.

applicability_as_implemented: model_directed_goal_pursuit false (no model, regex handlers), selects_or_sequences_actions false.
as_modeled: true, true (agent persona with tools, persistent memory, follows instructions).
